messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high GPU paging detected on r3-prod-2 (region us-west-2). auto-escalation to oncall.
oncall-ryan: Saw the alert, checking dashboards now. impact?
sre-maya: Errors up ~4-6% for text-generation endpoints, p99 latency spike to ~2.1s, small customer surface so far.
ml-runtime-lee: Uploading quick mem dump and batch traces to s3: s3://redwood-ops/triage/1765000000/ (link obfuscated). key files: gpu_stats.tsv, kv_cache_growth.log, request_trace.json
ml-runtime-lee: paste: ```
GPU0 free: 1.2GiB used: 30.8GiB total: 32GiB
Process peaks: 29.7GiB
KV cache entries: 2.1M -> +500k over last 2h
Page faults/sec: 180 -> spike coincident with heavy chat endpoint
```
prod-eng-sam: Hypothesis A: KV cache growth + long-tail seqs causing fragmentation and slow reclaim. Hypothesis B: batchsize increase in latest canary bumped mem pressure.
sre-maya: Can we try live mitigation: reduce default batch_size from 8 -> 4 on r3-prod-2 and enable immediate kv-eviction for prefixes >12h? low-risk rollout.
oncall-ryan: Doing a canary change now on 10% of pods. command: `rdctl route set env=r3-prod-2 batch_size=4 --selector=canary10`
support-ana: FYI two customers (acme, beta-co) reported intermittent 500s starting ~08:12 UTC. They're open to a brief maintenance window if needed.
cust-succ-oliver: Reaching out to ACME, they need ETA before we do anything that affects throughput.
ml-runtime-lee: After batch_size=4 canary: GPU paging drops ~55% on canary pods; KV cache still high but growth rate slowed. logs: `kv_cache_growth.log` shows #entries plateauing on canary.
sre-maya: Good. Rolling change to 50% while we keep watching. Also enabling kv eviction threshold: `kv_cache.eviction_age_ms=43200000` (12h) -> immediate rollout to all.
prod-eng-sam: Note: we changed quantization kernel in last deploy (PR #5123). Could contribute to slab fragmentation, keeping on radar.
oncall-ryan: Handoff to next oncall @sre-maya in 30m; leaving notes here. Customer impact assessed: partial for a few high-qps clients but no full outage.
support-ana: Logged impacted requests and TRACE IDs -> uploaded to ticket #INC-4891. Customers informed about ongoing mitigation.
sre-maya: Starting timeline build in the incident doc: https://docs.redwood.incidents/INC-4891/timeline (temporary link) — please drop any relevant logs there.
ml-runtime-lee: Added hypothesis table in doc: - H1 KV cache growth (evidence: +500k entries, plateau after batch reduce) - H2 slab fragmentation post-quant kernel change (evidence: allocator churn traces) - H3 batch-induced transient spikes (evidence: p99 reduction after batch_size down)
prod-eng-sam: Can someone run `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -l 1` on one of the effected hosts and attach a snapshot to the doc? quick grep of allocator histograms helpful.
ml-runtime-lee: Attached `allocator.hist` and `nvidia-smi.snap` to the timeline doc. short grep: `allocator: free_chunks: 12 small_slabs: 48 fragmented_slabs: 17`
oncall-ryan: Customer note: ACME ok with mitigations but asked for ETA on permanent fix. I'll coordinate with solutions.
sre-maya: Action items: 1) Keep batch_size=4 until full RCA (owner: sam). 2) Add periodic KV eviction policy to default (owner: lee). 3) Run defrag experiment on canary (owner: eng-runtime). 4) Postmortem draft in 48h (owner: ryan).
prod-eng-sam: I'll run controlled defrag test tonight in us-west-2 canary pool, capture before/after mem maps.
support-ana: Updating INC-4891 with customer comms and ETA: next update in 2h. :thumbsup:
ml-runtime-lee: Quick note: if defrag confirms fragmentation cause we'll propose a kernel rollback vs targeted reclaim patch. Both options scoped.
sre-maya: Last check 30m later: errors back down to baseline, p99 trending down. scheduling a follow-up postmortem call tomorrow 15:00 UTC.
oncall-ryan: Handoff complete — leaving a short runbook in the doc for the next oncall. :white_check_mark:
